claims: All fourteen direct dependencies are COMPLETE and bound in exact program order to their current cards, completion entries and hashes, and required Git coordinates.

The card assigns one worker and exactly six implementation, regression-test, and evidence files. Existing retained-source code, corpora, oracles, runtime, protocol, ledger, graph, and public package files are outside worker ownership.

The adapter receives only retained ModuleObservation and SourceClosure values. It may parse exact bytes, classify the closed LinkML 1.11.1 subset, cross-check authored imports, and emit immutable lossless per-module evidence or one typed atomic refusal.

One machine-readable profile owns source classification and one parser mechanism executes it. The Greenhouse bootstrap must delegate to that parser; a second parser, legacy path, or try-next fallback is forbidden.

Qualified binding, duplicate ownership and adoption decisions, hierarchy and default elaboration, canonical facts, artifacts, protocol-machine behavior, KnowledgeChangeSet construction, and runtime cutover remain later stages.

Quiet Bell is tested first for exact module and import evidence while its recorded missing import remains a full-compilation refusal. Greenhouse follows as a neutrality control, then feature cases close exact acceptance and refusal edges.

Candidate remains NONE, worker ledger remains NOT_STARTED, selections remain unchanged, and activation creates no adapter implementation, production test, worker evidence, public API, package, or fixture byte.
limitations: This verifies activation and boundary integrity only. It does not implement or complete the LinkML adapter.
The assigned worker must produce genuine implementation RED before production GREEN and retain the ordered TDD chain.
Public namespace, stable identifiers, autodoc, packaging, selection, promotion, and release remain separately governed.

summary: Verify the exact private LinkML adapter activation boundary.
why: Formal parser work starts only after dependency closure, one-profile authority, stage separation, exact worker scope, cumulative corpus order, genuine TDD, atomic refusal, and public-boundary deferrals are explicit and mechanically guarded.
